summary: The article is largely reliable, accurately reporting on the Income Tax Department's portal upgrades and key filing information for AY 2026-27.

claims.claim: The portal is now equipped to process up to 1 crore Income Tax Returns (ITRs) per day, ensuring greater efficiency.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the e-filing portal has been upgraded to process up to 1 crore (10 million) ITRs per day.

claims.claim: For most individual taxpayers, the deadline to file Income Tax Returns for Assessment Year 2026-27 (Financial Year 2025-26) is July 31, 2026.
claims.note: The deadline for most individual taxpayers (ITR-1 & ITR-2) for AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26) is indeed July 31, 2026. However, some categories like non-audit business cases (ITR-3 & ITR-4) have a deadline of August 31, 2026.

claims.claim: Missing the deadline can result in a late filing fee (up to ₹5,000 under Section 234F), loss of ability to carry forward certain losses, and potential interest under Section 234A on unpaid tax.
claims.note: Section 234F outlines late filing fees, which can be up to ₹5,000 (or ₹1,000 for income up to ₹5 lakh). Section 234A charges interest at 1% per month on unpaid tax. Loss carry-forward is also affected by late filing.

claims.claim: The interest under Section 234A on unpaid tax is 1% per month.
claims.note: Section 234A imposes interest at 1% per month or part thereof on the unpaid tax amount from the due date until the return is filed.

claims.claim: You can find your Annual Information Statement (AIS) and Taxpayer Information Summary (TIS) by logging into the e-filing portal (incometax.gov.in), navigating to the 'Services' tab, and selecting 'Annual Information Statement (AIS)'.
claims.note: This is the correct navigation path on the official Income Tax e-filing portal to access AIS.

claims.claim: Yes, the Income Tax Department typically provides offline utilities for various ITR forms. You can download these from the e-filing portal, prepare your return offline, and then upload the generated JSON file to the portal.
claims.note: The Income Tax Department provides offline utilities for ITR forms (e.g., ITR-1 to ITR-4) which can be downloaded from the e-filing portal. Returns can be prepared offline and then uploaded as a JSON file.

article_title: ITR Filing 2026: CBDT Upgrades Portal for Smoother Returns
